pyzed.App.desc:
Base class for applications (Elm architecture, like Iced). It is also the **main
window**, so it inherits everything from [`Window`](#window). Override `view()` and, if you use
messages, `update(message)`. State lives in instance attributes.

| Class attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `"Pyzed"` | Window title. Can be a callable (or property) that returns the text. |
| `size` | `(1280, 800)` | Initial window size. |
| `font_size` | `14` | Default text size. |
| `theme` | `themes.ONE_DARK` | A `Theme`, the name of a registered theme or `themes.auto(light, dark)`. Change it at any time. |
| `style` | `None` | The global style: a `pz.Style` for the whole window. Its text color, size, background, border color and radius become theme tokens. See [Styles](/pyzed/guides/styles/#the-global-style). |
| `system_dark` | `True` | Whether the system is in dark mode (updated by the runtime). |

The remaining window options (`min_size`, `resizable`, `decorations`, `scale`…) are on `Window`.

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `view()` | Returns the widget tree. Called after every message. |
| `update(message)` | Receives messages. Can return a `Command`, a list of them, a coroutine, a generator (regular or async) or another message. |
| `on_start()` | Optional. Runs once at startup; can return a `Command` or a coroutine. |
| `on_key(combo)` | Optional. Receives every key as `"ctrl-shift-p"`, `"escape"`, `"up"`… |
| `subscriptions()` | Optional. Returns the active subscriptions (`pz.every`, `pz.listen`). Re-evaluated after every `update`. |
| `resolved_theme()` | The concrete `Theme` in use (resolves names and `themes.auto`). |
| `run()` | Opens the window and blocks until the app exits. |
| `screenshot(path, *, size=None, scale=2.0, wait=0.1)` | Renders the current state to a PNG without a window. |

If `view()` raises an exception, the window shows the traceback instead of closing.

pyzed.run.desc: Runs an app: opens the window and blocks until it is closed. Accepts the class or an instance.

params.reload: Hot reload: saving a project file updates the running window and keeps its state. `None` follows `PYZED_RELOAD` (set by `pyzed dev`).
params.watch: Extra folders or files to watch for hot reload.

pyzed.screenshot.desc: Renders `app` offscreen (no window, no GPU) and saves a PNG. Useful for tests and documentation.

params.wait: Seconds to wait before capturing (for `on_start` tasks).

pyzed.post.desc: Sends a message to the running app from **any thread**. Raises `RuntimeError` if no app is running.

pyzed.load_font.desc: Loads an extra font (path to a `.ttf`/`.otf` or its bytes) so you can use it by family name: `text("hello", font="JetBrains Mono")`.

params.source: Path to the font file, or `bytes`.

pyzed.Window.desc:
An extra window with its own `view()`, title, size and theme. Open it by returning
`window.open()` (or `Command.open_window(window)`). Inside it, `self.app` is the app, so
windows share state; the messages it produces go to its `update()`, which by default
forwards them to `app.update()`.

| Attribute | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `"Pyzed"` | Text or callable. |
| `size` | `(800, 600)` | Initial size. |
| `min_size`, `max_size` | `None` | Size limits. |
| `position` | `None` | `"center"` or `(x, y)`. |
| `resizable` | `True` | Whether it can be resized. |
| `decorations` | `True` | `False` removes the system frame (custom title bar with `drag()`). |
| `transparent`, `maximized`, `fullscreen` | `False` | Initial state. |
| `scale` | `1.0` | UI scale. |
| `theme` | `None` | Its own theme; `None` uses the app's. |
| `style` | `None` | Its own global style; `None` uses the app's. |
| `app` | — | The app that owns the window (assigned when it opens). |
| `window_size` | — | Current size in logical pixels (updated by the runtime). |

| Method | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `view()` | Required. Returns the window's widget tree. |
| `update(message)` | Receives the window's messages (by default forwards them to the app). |
| `open()` / `close()` / `drag()` | Commands to open it, close it or start moving it. |
| `is_open` | Whether it is open. |
| `resolved_theme()` | The concrete `Theme` it uses. |
| `on_open()` | When it opens. |
| `on_close()` | When the user asks to close it; return `False` to prevent it. |
| `on_resize(width, height)` | When it is resized. |
| `on_key(combo)`, `subscriptions()` | As in `App`. |

pyzed.every.desc: A subscription that sends `message` to `update` every `seconds` seconds (like Iced's `time::every`). If `message` is a callable, it is called. Return it from `subscriptions()`.
pyzed.every.example:
def subscriptions(self):
                return [pz.every(1, "tick")] if self.running else []

pyzed.listen.desc: A subscription that runs `function()` (a generator or async generator) while it is active and sends every value it yields to `update`. Ideal for websockets and streams.
pyzed.listen.example:
async def feed():
                async for message in websocket:
                    yield message

            def subscriptions(self):
                return [pz.listen(feed)]

pyzed.Subscription.desc: What `every` and `listen` return. It is identified by its `key`: as long as `subscriptions()` keeps returning one with the same key, it keeps running; when it disappears, it stops.

pyzed.spawn.desc: Schedules a coroutine on Pyzed's asyncio loop without waiting for its result and returns a `concurrent.futures.Future`. To receive the result in the UI, return the coroutine from `update` or use `Command.perform`.

pyzed.asyncio_loop.desc: The asyncio loop (on a background thread) where Pyzed runs every coroutine. It starts the first time it is used.

pyzed.on.desc: Attaches common event handlers to a widget; same as `widget.on(...)`. Events: `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `mouse_down`, `mouse_up`, `mouse_enter`, `mouse_leave`, `mouse_move`, `scroll`, `drag_start`, `drag`, `drag_end`, `focus`, `blur`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `resize`. See [Events](/pyzed/guides/events/).

params.widget: The widget (a string is wrapped in a container).
params.cursor: Mouse cursor over the widget, such as `"pointer"` or `"grab"`.
params.handlers: `event=handler` pairs. A handler that takes an argument gets a `pz.Event`; a non-callable value is a message for `update`; `None` removes it.

pyzed.on.example: pz.container(card, padding=12).on(click=self.select, drag=lambda e: self.move(e.dx, e.dy))

pyzed.Event.desc: What happened, passed to event handlers: `type`, `x`, `y` (relative to the widget), `dx`, `dy` (scroll or drag movement), `width`, `height`, `button`, `key`, `shift`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `logo`, and `value`/`source` for custom events.

params.x: Pointer x, relative to the widget.
params.y: Pointer y, relative to the widget.

pyzed.Dock.desc: A Zed-style workspace: a `center` with `pz.DockPanel`s docked left, right, bottom or top. Users resize a side by dragging its inner edge and move a panel by dragging its tab onto a drop zone (or from the tab's right-click menu). `on_layout` receives the layout as a dict to save; pass it back as `layout=`. See [Layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/#docks-and-resizable-panels).

params.kwargs: Props and handlers by name, plus `key=`.
params.on_layout: Called with `event.value` = `{positions, sizes, active, hidden}` when panels move, resize or switch.

pyzed.Dock.example:
pz.Dock(center=editor, panels=[
                pz.DockPanel("project", "Project", tree, icon="folder", side="left"),
                pz.DockPanel("terminal", "Terminal", terminal, icon="terminal", side="bottom"),
            ], layout=self.layout, on_layout=lambda e: setattr(self, "layout", e.value))

params.id: Stable id (used in the saved layout).
params.title: Tab title.

pyzed.Component.desc: Base class for custom components, like React components: annotated class attributes are props, other attributes are state kept between renders, `render()` returns widgets and `events` declares custom events raised with `self.emit(name, value)`. Calling the class returns a widget. Components appear in the designer's toolbox. See [Custom components](/pyzed/guides/components/).

params.kwargs: Props by name, `on_<event>=` handlers (custom, lifecycle or common events) and `key=` to keep state when items move.

pyzed.Color.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds a color (a theme token or `"#rrggbb"`): the designer shows a color picker for it. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.Icon.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds a Lucide icon name: the designer shows an icon picker for it. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.Multiline.desc: Type hint for a component prop that holds long text: the designer shows a text area for it. A plain `str` at run time.

pyzed.Range.desc: Limits of a number prop, used with `typing.Annotated`: the designer shows a number box limited to them. See [Custom components](/pyzed/guides/components/#in-the-designer).

pyzed.state.desc: Declares a private state variable on a component class: the parent cannot pass it, and every instance starts with its own copy of the default (lists and dicts are safe). The designer lists it next to the props. See [Custom components](/pyzed/guides/components/).

params.default: Initial value, copied for each instance.

pyzed.component.LIFECYCLE_EVENTS.desc: Names of the lifecycle events every component raises (`mount`, `unmount`...).

pyzed.events.CATALOG.desc: Every event name Pyzed knows, mapped to its `EventInfo` (what raises it and what `event.value` holds).

pyzed.events.COMMON.desc: The events every widget accepts through `widget.on(...)` (click, hover, focus, keys...).

pyzed.t.desc: The text for `key` in the current language, formatted with `values`. Falls back from `"es_AR"` to `"es"`, then to the fallback language, then to the key. See [Languages](/pyzed/guides/i18n/).

params.language: Look it up in another language.
params.default: Returned when the key is missing (default: the key).
params.values: Values for `{name}` placeholders; `count=` also picks the plural form.

pyzed.t.example:
i18n.add("es", {"greeting": "¡Hola, {name}!", "files": {"one": "{count} archivo", "other": "{count} archivos"}})
            i18n.set_language("es")
            pz.t("greeting", name="Kev"), pz.t("files", count=3)

pyzed.i18n.add.desc: Adds or overrides texts for a language. Nested tables become dotted keys; `{"one": ..., "other": ...}` tables are plural forms.

pyzed.i18n.load.desc: Loads every `<language>.json` and `<language>.toml` in `folder`; returns the languages found.

pyzed.i18n.set_language.desc: Switches the language. The app shows it on its next render, so call it from a handler.

pyzed.i18n.set_fallback.desc: The language used when a text is missing (default `"en"`).

pyzed.i18n.on_change.desc: Calls `listener(language)` after every switch; returns a function that removes it.

params.listener: Callable that receives the new language.

pyzed.i18n.system_language.desc: The operating system's language (`LANG`, `LC_ALL` or the locale).

params.default: Returned when the system reports none.

pyzed.i18n.has.desc: Whether `key` has a text in the language or its fallbacks.

params.language: Language to check (default: the current one).

pyzed.Command.desc: The command class. Don't instantiate it directly: use its static methods.

params.id: The `id` you passed to the widget.

pyzed.Command.select_all.desc: Focuses the `text_input` with that `id` and selects all its text (typing replaces it).

pyzed.Command.set_editor_text.desc: Replaces the content of the `code_editor` with that `id`. Editors are uncontrolled: `text` is only the initial value.

pyzed.Command.set_editor_cursor.desc: Moves the editor cursor (line and column start at 1). Works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

pyzed.Command.fold_all.desc: Folds every block of the editor (`fold=False` unfolds them all). Works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

pyzed.Command.fold_line.desc: Folds (or unfolds) the block that starts at `line`, by indentation. Works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

pyzed.Command.editor_action.desc: Runs a named editor action in the editor with that `id`, as if its key was pressed: Zed's action name in snake case (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`, `"move_line_up"`, `"toggle_comments"`…). Raises `ValueError` for an unknown name.

params.name: The action's name (`Command.editor_actions()` lists them; `"editor::SelectNext"` works too).

pyzed.Command.select_editor_ranges.desc: Selects ranges of the editor, one cursor each; the first one is the primary cursor. Unfolds what hides them and works even if the editor hasn't been drawn yet.

params.ranges: `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends (an empty range is a plain cursor).

pyzed.Command.replace_editor_ranges.desc: Replaces ranges of the editor with texts as one undo step, and calls the editor's `on_change` (search and replace).

params.edits: `[((line, column, end_line, end_column), text)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends.

pyzed.Command.scroll_to_end.desc: Scrolls the `scrollable` with that `id` to the end.

pyzed.Command.message.desc: Sends `message` to `update` again on the next cycle.

pyzed.Command.perform.desc: Runs `function()` in the background and delivers the result to `then(result)` on the UI thread. `function` can be regular (runs on a thread) or `async def` (runs on Pyzed's asyncio loop). If it returns a generator (regular or async), `then` is called with each value. It also accepts an already created coroutine or generator (`fetch(url)` instead of `fetch`). Without `then`, results go to `update`. If `function` raises, the error is printed.

params.function: Function with no arguments that does the slow work.
params.then: Callable that receives the result (or `None` to send it to `update`).

pyzed.Command.scroll_to.desc: Scrolls the `scrollable` with that `id` to an absolute position in pixels.

pyzed.Command.paste.desc: Reads the clipboard and calls `then(text)` (empty string if it is empty).

pyzed.Command.open_window.desc: Opens a new window for that `pz.Window` instance.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.drag_window.desc: Starts moving the window with the mouse (use it when a custom title bar is pressed).

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.
The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.toggle_maximize_window.desc: Maximizes the window, or restores it if it already is.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.
The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.
The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.move_window.desc: Moves the window to a position on the screen.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Command.focus_window.desc: Brings the window to the front and focuses it.

params.window: The window (`pz.Window`). Without it, the one that produced the message.

pyzed.Widget.desc:
An immutable node of the UI tree, implemented in Rust. Returned by every widget and component function. Wherever a child is expected you can also pass a string or a number (converted to `text`) or `None` (ignored).

Every widget has `widget.on(...)` (see [Events](/pyzed/guides/events/)) and `widget.style(*styles, **props)`, which styles it like CSS: background, borders, radius, shadow, padding, margin, size and the typography of every text inside. `widget.style_props()` returns what was set. See [Styles](/pyzed/guides/styles/).

pyzed.container.desc: Wraps a child to give it size, alignment, background, border, radius and shadow.

params.content: The child (or `None` for an empty box, handy as a colored rectangle).
params.center: Centers the content on both axes and fills all the space.

pyzed.center.desc: Centers `content` in all the available space. Equivalent to `container(content, center=True)`.

params.anchor_bottom: Keeps the scroll pinned to the end (logs, terminals, chats).
params.margin: Margin between the scrollbar and the content.
params.on_scroll: Callable that receives a dict with `x`, `y`, `relative_x`, `relative_y`, `width`, `height`, `content_width` and `content_height`.

pyzed.stack.desc: Layers its children on top of each other, the last one on top. The basis for layers, modals and notifications.

pyzed.space.desc: Empty space of a given size.

pyzed.hspace.desc: Flexible horizontal gap: pushes the siblings in a row towards the edges.

pyzed.vspace.desc: Flexible vertical gap: pushes the siblings in a column towards the edges.

pyzed.rule.extra: A horizontal rule fills the full width. Inside a column that should shrink, set `width="shrink"` on the column.

pyzed.grid.desc: Lays out its children in a grid. With `columns=3` the columns are equal (or `max_width` fits as many as possible). With track lists (`columns=[200, "1fr", "auto"]`, `rows=...`) it works like a CSS grid: numbers are pixels, `"auto"` fits the content and `"<n>fr"` shares the space left. Wrap children in `pz.cell` to place them and make them span; the rest fill the free cells row by row. See [Layout](/pyzed/guides/layout/#grids).

params.columns: Number of equal columns, or tracks: a list (`[200, "1fr", "auto"]`) or a string (`"200 1fr auto"`).
params.rows: Row tracks, like `columns`. Rows beyond the list are `"auto"`.
params.height: With `columns=<int>`: height of each row. With tracks: the grid's height.
params.width: With `columns=<int>`: pixels. With tracks: the grid's width (default `"fill"`).
params.aspect_ratio: Keeps cells at this width/height ratio (`columns=<int>` only).
params.max_width: Fits as many columns of at most this width as possible (`columns=<int>` only).
params.align_x: Horizontal alignment of items in their cells: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`.
params.align_y: Vertical alignment of items in their cells.

pyzed.grid.example:
pz.grid([pz.cell(header, column=0, row=0, column_span=2), sidebar, content],
                    columns=[200, "1fr"], rows=[48, "1fr"], spacing=8, height="fill")

pyzed.cell.desc: Places a child in a track grid: its column and row (from 0) and how many it spans. Children without a cell fill the free cells row by row. Outside a grid it is just the child.

pyzed.flex.desc: Lays children out along one axis, like CSS flexbox, with `justify` on the main axis and `align` on the cross axis. Use `pz.flex_item` to make a child grow or give it a fixed size.

params.children: The widgets, or `pz.flex_item(...)` for children with their own sizing.
params.justify: `"start"`, `"center"`, `"end"`, `"between"`, `"around"` or `"evenly"`. No effect when a child grows.
params.wrap: Wraps onto new lines (rows with `justify="start"` only).

pyzed.flex.example: pz.flex([logo, title, pz.flex_item(search, grow=1), avatar], justify="between", align="center", gap=8)

params.grow: Share of the free space on the main axis (`0` keeps its natural size).
params.basis: A fixed main size in pixels, instead of growing.

pyzed.resizable.desc: A panel whose `edge` can be dragged to resize it. It keeps the size the user drags it to; `on_resize(size)` is called when a drag ends so you can save it. Changing `size` later resets it.

params.edge: The edge with the handle: `"right"` (a left sidebar), `"left"`, `"top"` (a bottom panel) or `"bottom"`.
params.on_resize: Called with the new size when a drag ends.
params.hover_color: Line color while hovered or dragged.
params.handle: Width of the area that can be grabbed.

pyzed.split.desc: Two panes with a draggable divider. For the theme style use `ui.split`.

params.ratio: Proportion of the first pane (0–1). The split keeps the ratio the user drags to until this changes.
params.on_resize: Callable that receives the new ratio while dragging.
params.min_size: Minimum size of the first pane.
params.min_size_second: Minimum size of the second pane.
params.hover_color: Divider color on hover or while dragging.

pyzed.pin.desc: Places `content` at `(x, y)` inside a box. Use it in a `stack` to position popovers and context menus.

pyzed.responsive.desc: Builds its content with `function(width, height)` using the space actually available, so the layout can adapt (for example, hiding a sidebar when the window is narrow).

params.function: Function that receives `(width, height)` and returns a widget.

params.font: `"sans"` (IBM Plex Sans), `"mono"`, `"icons"`, `"serif"` or the name of a family loaded with `load_font`.
params.line_height: Line height relative to the size (1.0, 1.5…).
params.wrap: Line wrapping. With `False` the text doesn't wrap.

pyzed.icon.desc: A [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) icon. `color` defaults to the surrounding text color.

params.source: Path to an `.svg`, the SVG code as a string (starting with `<`) or `bytes`.
params.color: If given, tints the whole SVG with that color (useful for monochrome icons).

pyzed.image.desc: A bitmap image (PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, WebP…) from a path or `bytes`, or raw RGBA pixels.

params.size: `(width, height)` when `source` is raw RGBA pixels.

pyzed.image_viewer.desc: An image you can pan (by dragging) and zoom (mouse wheel), like Iced's viewer.

params.scale_step: How much the zoom changes per wheel step.

pyzed.markdown.desc: Renders Markdown (headings, lists, code blocks, quotes, tables, links…). For the theme colors use `ui.markdown`.

params.on_link: Callable that receives the URL when a link is clicked.

pyzed.rich_text.desc: Text made of spans with different styles. Plain strings are unstyled spans.
pyzed.rich_text.example: pz.rich_text(["Click ", pz.span("here", color="#74ade8", underline=True, link=self.open), " to open."])

pyzed.span.desc: A styled span for `rich_text`. With `link`, clicking it sends (or calls) that value.

pyzed.Span.desc: The type of the spans created by `pz.span`.

params.data: The text or URL to encode.
params.cell_size: Size of each module in pixels.

pyzed.canvas.desc: A 2D drawing surface. `shapes` is a list created with [`pyzed.draw`](/pyzed/reference/draw/). Mouse callbacks receive coordinates relative to the canvas. With an `id`, the geometry is cached between frames and only recomputed when the shapes change. See the [drawing with canvas](/pyzed/guides/canvas/) guide.

params.shapes: List of `pyzed.draw` shapes (nested lists are accepted).
params.on_press: Callable that receives `(x, y)` on press.
params.on_release: Callable that receives `(x, y)` on release.
params.on_right_press: Callable that receives `(x, y)` on right click.
params.on_scroll: Callable that receives `(dx, dy)` in lines when the wheel is used.

pyzed.button.desc: A button with no predefined style. For the Zed button use `ui.button`.

pyzed.text_input.desc: A controlled text field: it shows `value` and notifies you of changes through `on_input`. For the Zed style use `ui.input`.

pyzed.mouse_area.desc: Detects mouse events over its content.

params.on_scroll: Callable that receives `(dx, dy)` in lines when the wheel is used.

pyzed.hover.desc: Shows `top` over `base` only while the mouse is over it (for example, a tab's close button).

pyzed.opaque.desc: Makes a widget block the mouse for whatever is below it in a `stack`.

pyzed.tooltip.desc: Shows `tip` next to `content` on hover. `ui.tooltip` adds the Zed style.

params.on_release: Sent when the knob is released.

pyzed.pick_list.desc: A dropdown to choose one of `options`. `on_select(option)` receives the chosen one. For the Zed style use `ui.select`.

pyzed.radio.desc: A radio button. Group several yourself (or use `ui.radio_group`); `on_select` is sent when it is clicked.

params.spacing: Space between the circle and the text.

pyzed.code_editor.desc:
A code editor with syntax highlighting, line numbers and git markers, based on Iced's
`text_editor`. It is **uncontrolled**: `text` is only the initial value for that `id`; the
text, cursor and history live in Rust. Use `Command.set_editor_text` to replace it.
For the Zed style use [`ui.editor`](/pyzed/components/code/).

params.id: Identifies the buffer. Reuse it to keep state across renders.
params.syntax: Map of TextMate scopes to colors (provided by `Theme.syntax_scopes()`).
params.gutter_active_color: Color of the cursor line's number.
params.markers: `{line: color}` for git markers in the gutter (lines from 1).
params.on_change: Callable that receives the full text after each edit.
params.annotations: `{line: "text"}` or `{line: ("text", color)}`: virtual text at the end of the line (code lens, diagnostics).
params.whitespace: Draws spaces as `·` and tabs as `→` in this color.
params.tab_size: Tab inserts spaces up to the next multiple; Enter keeps the indentation; Backspace removes a level.
params.capture_keys: Keys the editor leaves to the app's `on_key` (`"up"`, `"enter"`…), e.g. while a completion list is open.
params.auto_close: Typing a bracket or quote also inserts its closing pair.
params.folding: Fold chevrons in the gutter and Ctrl+Shift+[ / ].
params.minimap: Width of the minimap in pixels (`None`: no minimap).
params.minimap_thumb: Color of the minimap's visible-area highlight.
params.on_zoom: Callable that receives `1`, `-1` or `0` for Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+wheel.
params.on_action: Callable that receives the name of each editor action that runs (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`…).
params.highlights: Ranges painted behind the text (search results): `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends.
params.match_brackets: Outlines the bracket that matches the one next to the cursor.
params.selection_highlight: Highlights the other occurrences of the selected text.

pyzed.Style.desc: A reusable set of style properties for `widget.style(...)`, a component's `style=` or `App.style`. Combine styles with `|` (the right one wins). See [Styles](/pyzed/guides/styles/).

params.styles: Styles, dicts or style names to start from.
params.props: Properties: `background`, `color`, `font`, `weight`, `italic`, `size`, `line_height`, `border_color`, `border_width`, `border` (`(width, color)`), `radius`, `shadow`, `padding`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `align_x`, `align_y`, `clip`. Colors may be theme tokens.

pyzed.Style.example:
card = pz.Style(background="panel", border=(1, "border"), radius=8, padding=12)
            pz.column([...]).style(card | pz.Style(shadow=("#0006", (0, 4), 12)))

pyzed.define_style.desc: Names a style so widgets can use it by name: `widget.style("card")`. Returns it.

pyzed.set_style.desc: Sets the global style for every window, under each window's `style`. Without arguments it clears it.

pyzed.Gradient.desc: A linear gradient for backgrounds. Angles follow CSS: 0 up, 90 right, 180 (the default) down. Up to 8 stops.

params.stops: Colors, spread evenly, or `(offset, color)` pairs with offsets from 0 to 1.

pyzed.Mask.desc: An opacity mask for a `Paint`: how visible the fill is along a direction. On a gradient it follows the gradient's direction.

params.stops: Opacities (0 to 1), spread evenly, or `(offset, opacity)` pairs.
params.angle: Direction when the fill is a plain color.

pyzed.Paint.desc: A fill: a color or `Gradient` with an overall opacity and an optional `Mask`. Works anywhere a background does.

params.opacity: 0 to 1, multiplies the fill's own alpha.

pyzed.Paint.example: pz.Paint("#3b82f6", opacity=0.8, mask=pz.Mask([1, 0]))  # fades out downwards

params.color: Theme token or hex color. Defaults to `"text"`.

pyzed.ui.icon_button.desc: A square button with just an icon (Zed's `IconButton`).

pyzed.ui.badge.desc: A small pill for statuses and counters.

pyzed.ui.indicator.desc: A colored dot (status, unsaved changes, presence).

pyzed.ui.kbd.desc: Draws a shortcut as keys: `"ctrl-shift-p"`, `"cmd-k cmd-s"`. Uses symbols on macOS (⌘⇧P) and words elsewhere.

pyzed.ui.format_keys.desc: Splits a shortcut into labels per chord: `format_keys("ctrl-shift-p") == [["Ctrl", "Shift", "P"]]`. The style is controlled by `pyzed.ui.base.KEY_STYLE` (`"auto"`, `"symbols"` or `"words"`).

params.index: Picks a collaborator color from the theme (`theme.players`).

pyzed.ui.tooltip.desc: Wraps `content` with a Zed-style tooltip, optionally with its shortcut.

pyzed.ui.divider.desc: A divider line in the theme color.

pyzed.ui.card.desc: A bordered surface to group content, with an optional title and actions.

params.borderless: No border or background (as in the command palette).

pyzed.ui.search_input.desc: An `input` with a magnifying glass icon.

pyzed.ui.segmented.desc: A group of mutually exclusive buttons (Zed's `ToggleButtonGroup`).

pyzed.ui.field.desc: A form row: title and description on the left, control on the right (like Zed's settings).

pyzed.ui.dialog_layer.desc: Shows a dialog centered over `base` with a dimmed backdrop. With `dialog=None` it returns `base` unchanged, so it can always wrap the view. See [Dialogs](/pyzed/guides/i18n/#dialogs).

params.dialog: A dialog from the functions below, or `ui.modal`.
params.on_dismiss: Sent when the backdrop is clicked.

pyzed.ui.dialog_layer.example:
ui.dialog_layer(self.main_view(), ui.confirm("Delete 3 files?", self.delete, self.cancel, danger=True)
                            if self.asking else None, on_dismiss=self.cancel)

params.on_close: The button and the close icon.

params.danger: Paints the confirm button red and labels it Delete.

pyzed.ui.prompt.desc: Asks for a line of text.

pyzed.ui.choice.desc: A message with your own buttons.

params.options: `(label, on_press)` pairs; the last one is the main button.

pyzed.ui.unsaved_changes.desc: "Save your changes to *name* before closing?" with Don't save, Cancel and Save.

pyzed.ui.select.desc: A dropdown with the theme style (Zed's `DropdownMenu`). Options are displayed with `str()`, so strings, enums or dataclasses all work.

pyzed.ui.radio_group.desc: Mutually exclusive options as radio buttons.

params.on_select: Callable that receives the chosen value.
params.horizontal: In a row instead of a column.

pyzed.ui.number_field.desc: A numeric field with −/+ buttons (Zed's `NumericStepper`). `on_change(value)` receives the number already clamped to `min`/`max`; anything that can't be parsed as a number is ignored.

params.align: Where the number sits between the buttons: `"center"` (default), `"start"` or `"end"`.

pyzed.ui.split_button.desc: A button with a separate arrow for more options (Zed's `SplitButton`). `on_press` runs the main action and `on_menu` usually opens a `ui.menu` in a `ui.popover`.

pyzed.ui.chip.desc: A compact tag, optionally clickable (filters) and with a button to remove it.

params.on_remove: Shows a ✕ that sends this when clicked.

pyzed.ui.disclosure.desc: A collapsible section: a header with an arrow that shows or hides `content`. You own the open state: change it in `on_toggle`.

params.title: Title (text or widget).
params.on_toggle: Message or callable when the header is clicked.

pyzed.ui.AccordionSection.desc: One section of `ui.accordion`: `key`, `title`, `content` and optional `icon` and header `end` widget.

pyzed.ui.accordion.desc: Stacked collapsible sections separated by dividers, like the panels of Zed's settings. Each header spans the whole width, so the content lines up with the rest of the panel. You own the open state: change it in `on_toggle`.

params.sections: `ui.AccordionSection(key, title, content, icon=None, end=None)` items (or `(key, title, content)` tuples).
params.open: The set of open ids, a `{id: bool}` dict, or `True` for all.
params.on_toggle: Called with the key of the clicked header.
params.icons: `{id: icon}`: a Lucide icon for each header.
params.spacing: Space around the dividers between sections.
params.padding: Padding around the content of an open section.

pyzed.ui.accordion.example:
ui.accordion([
                ui.AccordionSection("layout", "Layout", layout_rows, icon="ruler"),
                ui.AccordionSection("events", "Events", event_rows, icon="zap"),
            ], open=self.open_sections, on_toggle=lambda key: self.open_sections.symmetric_difference_update({key}))

pyzed.ui.Log.desc: The entries of a `ui.console`: thread-safe, capped at `limit`, with repeated lines folded into one. `write(level, text)` adds a line; `capture()` (or `with log:`) copies `print` output and tracebacks into it; `pipe(stream)` reads a subprocess's output in a background thread; `text()` returns everything for copying.

params.on_write: Called after every write (from any thread).

pyzed.ui.Log.example:
log = ui.Log()
            with log:
                print("hello")          # still reaches the terminal
            ui.console(log.entries, on_clear=log.clear)

pyzed.ui.LogEntry.desc: One line of a `ui.Log`: `level`, `text`, `time`, `count` (identical lines in a row) and `clock` (`HH:MM:SS`).

pyzed.ui.LOG_LEVELS.desc: The levels `ui.console` colors, in the order of its filter buttons: info, event, stdout, stderr, warning, error.

pyzed.ui.console.desc: A log view like a browser's dev tools console: a filter box, one toggle per level with its count, copy and clear, and the entries in a monospace list that keeps scrolling to the newest one.

params.on_query: Receives each edit of the filter.
params.on_toggle_level: Called with the level of the clicked toggle.
params.actions: Extra widgets at the end of the toolbar.

pyzed.ui.shortcuts.desc: A searchable list of key bindings, grouped (for a Keyboard shortcuts dialog).

pyzed.ui.about.desc: An About box: icon, name, version, a description, a few details and link buttons.

params.title: Title (text or widget).
params.tint: `"info"`, `"success"`, `"warning"`, `"error"` or `"hint"`: picks the color and icon.

pyzed.ui.empty_state.desc: A centered placeholder for empty lists, searches with no results, etc.

pyzed.ui.settings_group.desc: A titled block of `ui.field` rows separated by lines (Zed's settings UI).

pyzed.ui.Column.desc: A column of `ui.table`. `key` is a dict key, an attribute name or a function of the row; `render` (optional) turns the value into a widget. `width` is `"fill"`, a number or `("fill", 2)`.

params.title: Header (and name used for sorting).
params.key: How to get the value from each row.
params.sortable: Whether the header can be clicked to sort.

pyzed.ui.table.desc: A data table with a fixed header, optional sorting and row selection. Sorting happens here when `sort_by` names a column: clicking a header calls `on_sort(title)` and you update `sort_by`/`descending` in your state.

params.sort_by: Title of the column to sort by.
params.on_sort: Callable that receives the clicked title.
params.on_row_press: Callable that receives the clicked row.

pyzed.ui.stat.desc: A dashboard number: title, large value, optional change (`+4.2%`) and sparkline.

params.title: Title.
params.delta: Change in %; green if positive, red otherwise.

pyzed.ui.sparkline.desc: A tiny line chart for trends.

params.fill: Fills the area under the line.

pyzed.ui.bar_chart.desc: A vertical bar chart with optional labels.

pyzed.ui.donut.desc: A donut chart; `label` is drawn in the center.

pyzed.ui.spinner.desc: A spinning arc for loading states. Its angle comes from the clock, so keep a `pz.every(1/30, ...)` subscription active while it is shown.

pyzed.ui.count_badge.desc: A round counter (notifications, problems…). Shows `99+` above `max`.

pyzed.ui.facepile.desc: Overlapping collaborator avatars, as in Zed's title bar. Those beyond `max_shown` are grouped into `+N`.

pyzed.ui.keybinding_hint.desc: A muted hint like “Open file Ctrl P” for footers and empty states.

pyzed.ui.markdown.desc: `pz.markdown` with the theme's text, link and code colors.

params.on_link: Callable that receives the URL when a link is clicked.

pyzed.ui.split.desc: `pz.split` with the divider in the theme's border color (accent while dragging).

params.on_resize: Callable that receives the new ratio.

pyzed.ui.list_item.desc: A list row (Zed's `ListItem`): icon, text and a slot at the end.

params.inset: With margin and rounded corners (menus, palettes).

pyzed.ui.TreeNode.desc: A file or folder for `ui.tree`. Folders have `children` (a list). `status` is `"modified"`, `"created"`, `"deleted"`, `"conflict"` or `"ignored"`. `TreeNode.from_paths(paths, status=None)` builds the tree from paths like `"src/main.rs"`, with folders first and the git status propagated to folders.

pyzed.ui.tree.desc: A collapsible file tree (Zed's project panel).

params.on_toggle: Called with the id of the clicked folder.
params.on_select: Called with the id of the clicked file.

params.checked: Shows a check mark (`True`/`False`) or nothing (`None`).

pyzed.ui.menu.desc: A floating context menu. Use `ui.SEPARATOR` between groups; a plain string is a header.

pyzed.ui.Tab.desc: A tab. `Tab.for_file(path, **kwargs)` creates it with the file's name and icon.

pyzed.ui.tab.desc: A single tab. You normally use `tab_bar`.

params.active: Whether it is the active one.

pyzed.ui.tab_bar.desc: A row of tabs with optional controls at the start and end (navigation, split, +). The close button appears on the active tab and on hover.

pyzed.ui.breadcrumbs.desc: `src › main.rs › fn main`. Parts can be strings or `(icon, text)` tuples.

params.on_press: Called with the index of the clicked part.

pyzed.ui.toolbar.desc: The bar below the tabs: breadcrumbs on the left and buffer actions on the right.

pyzed.ui.workspace.desc: The layout of a Zed window: title bar, left, right and bottom docks, center and status bar. Pass `None` to hide a dock.

params.on_resize: Called with `(side, size)` when the user finishes resizing a dock by dragging its inner border.

pyzed.ui.title_bar.desc: The top bar: project and branch pickers on the left, account and actions on the right.

pyzed.ui.title_button.desc: A compact button for the title bar (`pyzed ▾`, `main`…).

pyzed.ui.status_item.desc: An icon and/or text in the status bar (diagnostics, cursor position, language…).

pyzed.ui.panel.desc: A dockable panel. `side` decides which edge gets the border line; with a numeric `width` (`height` for the bottom) that border can be dragged to resize it.

params.on_resize: Called with the new size when a drag ends.

pyzed.ui.panel_header.desc: A panel header: icon, title and actions.

pyzed.ui.layer.desc: Stacks `overlay` on top of `base`. Clicking outside sends `on_dismiss`. With `overlay=None` it returns `base` unchanged.

params.overlay: What floats on top (modal, palette, menu).
params.backdrop: Color of the backdrop that dims the UI.
params.offset: Distance from the top when `align_y` is `"start"`.

pyzed.ui.modal.desc: A dialog. Use it as the `overlay` of `ui.layer`.

params.footer: Footer buttons, aligned to the right.

params.detail: Secondary text (for example, a file path).

pyzed.ui.command_palette.desc: Zed's command palette: fuzzy-filters `commands` by `query` and shows their shortcuts.

params.on_query: Callable that receives the new text.

pyzed.ui.picker.desc: A searchable list on a floating surface. The basis of the palette and the file finder.

params.on_query: Callable that receives the new text.
params.empty_text: Text shown when there are no results.

pyzed.ui.fuzzy_match.desc: Returns `(score, positions)` if every letter of `query` appears in order in `candidate`; otherwise `None`. Rewards word starts and consecutive letters.

pyzed.ui.fuzzy_filter.desc: Filters and sorts `items` by fuzzy score. Returns `[(item, positions), ...]`.

params.key: Function that returns the text of each item.

pyzed.ui.highlighted.desc: Text with the characters at `positions` highlighted (fuzzy search matches).

pyzed.ui.toasts.desc: Shows `items` (usually `toast(...)`) stacked in the bottom-right corner over `base`.

pyzed.ui.popover.desc: Shows `content` (a `ui.menu`, a card…) over `base` at `(x, y)`. Clicking anywhere else calls `on_dismiss`. For a right-click menu, store the mouse position with `mouse_area(on_move=...)` and open the popover from `on_right_press` (see `examples/context_menu.py`).

pyzed.ui.editor.desc: Zed's code editor: highlighting with the theme colors, line numbers and git markers.

params.id: Identifies the buffer (use the file path).
params.language: Language. If missing, it is inferred from `path`.
params.annotations: `{line: "text"}` or `{line: ("text", color)}`: virtual text at the end of the line (code lens, diagnostics).
params.show_whitespace: Draws spaces as `·` and tabs as `→`.
params.tab_size: Tab inserts spaces up to the next multiple; Enter keeps the indentation (one more level after `:`); Backspace removes a level.
params.capture_keys: Keys the editor leaves to the app's `on_key` (`"up"`, `"enter"`…), e.g. while a completion list is open.
params.auto_close: Closes brackets and quotes as you type (and wraps the selection).
params.folding: Fold chevrons in the gutter; Ctrl+Shift+[ folds and Ctrl+Shift+] unfolds.
params.minimap: `True` (or a width in pixels) shows a minimap on the right.
params.cursor_color: Cursor color (the theme's player color by default).
params.on_zoom: Callable that receives `1`, `-1` or `0` for Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- / Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+wheel.
params.on_action: Callable that receives the name of each editor action that runs (`"undo"`, `"select_next"`…), e.g. to count them.
params.highlights: Ranges painted behind the text in the theme's search color: `[(line, column, end_line, end_column)]`, from 1, with exclusive ends.
params.match_brackets: Outlines the bracket that matches the one next to the cursor (Ctrl+M jumps to it).
params.selection_highlight: Highlights the other occurrences of the selected text (Ctrl+D adds the next one as a cursor).

pyzed.ui.language_token.desc: Returns the highlighter language token for a path (`"main.rs"` → `"rs"`).

pyzed.ui.terminal.desc: A read-only terminal view with ANSI colors. It stays scrolled to the end.

params.lines: Text with ANSI escapes, or a list of lines of `(text, color)` segments.

pyzed.ui.ansi.desc: Converts text with ANSI colors into lines of `(text, color_name)` segments.

pyzed.ui.ColorPicker.desc: A component that picks a color with alpha, a linear gradient (stops you add, drag and remove, plus an angle) or a fill with an opacity mask. `on_change` gets a `"#rrggbb[aa]"` string, a `pz.Gradient` or a `pz.Paint`, all valid as a `background`. Pass the picked value back as `value`. See [Styles](/pyzed/guides/styles/#color-picker).

params.alpha: Shows the alpha bar and field.
params.swatches: Quick colors (default: the theme's accent and status colors).

pyzed.ui.color_swatch.desc: A small square showing a color, gradient or paint over a checkerboard.

pyzed.ui.checkerboard.desc: A light/dark checkerboard to draw under translucent colors.

pyzed.Theme.desc: A theme: an immutable dataclass with Zed's color tokens (surfaces, borders, elements, text, status, editor, syntax, collaborator and ANSI colors) and metrics (`radius`, `radius_sm`, `ui_font_size`, `buffer_font_size`). The `is_dark` property tells whether it is dark.

pyzed.Theme.derive.desc: Returns a copy with some tokens changed. The `syntax` and `ansi` dicts are merged instead of replaced.

pyzed.Theme.color.desc: Resolves a token (`"accent"`, `"text_muted"`…) to its color. Hex colors and `"transparent"` pass through unchanged.

pyzed.Theme.syntax_scopes.desc: Maps Zed's syntax tokens to TextMate scopes for the highlighter.

pyzed.Theme.palette.desc: The base palette passed to Iced for its internal styles. Internal use.

pyzed.Theme.with_accent.desc: A copy with a different accent color and everything that depends on it (focus, selection, links, primary buttons, text on accent).

pyzed.Theme.generate.desc: Creates a complete theme from a few colors. Surfaces, borders, hover states and muted text are mixed from `background` and `text`; the appearance is inferred from the background brightness if not given.

pyzed.Theme.from_zed.desc: Reads a theme from a Zed theme family file (`.json`) or a dict. A family usually has several (Ayu Dark/Light/Mirage); `name` picks one (the first by default).

params.name: Name of the theme within the family.

pyzed.Theme.to_dict.desc: A JSON-ready dict; `Theme.from_dict` reads it back.

pyzed.Theme.from_dict.desc: Creates a theme from `to_dict`. Missing tokens come from `base` (One Dark or One Light depending on `appearance`).

pyzed.Theme.save.desc: Saves the theme as JSON (Pyzed's own format).

pyzed.Theme.load.desc: Reads a theme written with `save` (for Zed themes use `from_zed`).

pyzed.themes.desc: Namespace with the built-in themes (Zed's One, Ayu and Gruvbox families) and the theme registry. Built-in themes are also available as attributes: `themes.ONE_DARK`, `themes.ONE_LIGHT`, `themes.AYU_DARK`, `themes.AYU_LIGHT`, `themes.AYU_MIRAGE`, `themes.GRUVBOX_DARK`, `themes.GRUVBOX_LIGHT`…

pyzed.themes.get.desc: Looks up a theme by name (case-insensitive). Raises `KeyError` if it doesn't exist.

pyzed.themes.register.desc: Adds (or replaces) a theme so it can be used by name.

pyzed.themes.load_zed.desc: Loads and registers every theme in a Zed family file.

pyzed.themes.auto.desc: A theme that follows the system's light/dark mode.

pyzed.AutoTheme.desc: What `themes.auto` returns: a `(light, dark)` pair. `pick(dark)` returns the right one.

pyzed.theme.current.desc: The theme components use when no `theme=` is passed.

pyzed.theme.use.desc: Changes the current theme. `App` does this before every `view()`, so you normally don't need it.

pyzed.theme.alpha.desc: Returns `color` with its opacity multiplied by `value`.

pyzed.theme.mix.desc: Mixes two colors: `amount=0` is `a` and `amount=1` is `b`.

pyzed.theme.resolve.desc: Turns an `App.theme` value (theme, name, `AutoTheme` or `None`) into a `Theme`.

params.dark: Whether the system is in dark mode.

pyzed.theme.luminance.desc: Relative luminance (WCAG) of a color, from 0 to 1.

pyzed.theme.contrast.desc: WCAG contrast ratio between two colors (1 to 21).

pyzed.theme.readable_on.desc: Returns `light` or `dark`, whichever has more contrast on `background`.

pyzed.icons.icon.desc: An icon widget. Also available as `pyzed.icon`.

pyzed.icons.glyph.desc: Returns an icon's character, to use in any text with `font="icons"`. Raises `ValueError` if it doesn't exist.

pyzed.icons.names.desc: Sorted list of all icon names.

pyzed.icons.for_file.desc: Returns `(icon, color_or_None)` for a file name, as in Zed's project panel.

pyzed.icons.language_for.desc: Human-readable language name of a file (`"main.py"` → `"Python"`), handy for the status bar.

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.rects.desc: Many rectangles filled with one color in a single shape (fast for grids and bars).

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.
`"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.polyline.desc: Joins `points` with straight lines (`closed=True` closes the shape).

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.
`"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.arc.desc: A circular arc from `start` to `end` degrees (0 = 3 o'clock, clockwise). `pie=True` closes it through the center (pie slice).

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.path.desc: A free-form path with SVG-like operations: `("M", x, y)` move, `("L", x, y)` line, `("Q", cx, cy, x, y)` quadratic curve, `("C", c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, x, y)` cubic curve, `("A", cx, cy, r, start, end)` arc, `("Z",)` close.

params.cap: `"round"`, `"square"` or `"butt"`: shape of the line ends.

pyzed.draw.text.desc: Text anchored at `(x, y)`; `align_x`/`align_y` choose which side of the text sits on that point.

pyzed.draw.translate.desc: Offsets the shapes that come after it.

pyzed.draw.rotate.desc: Rotates the shapes that come after it around the current origin.

pyzed.draw.scale.desc: Scales the shapes that come after it.

pyzed.draw.save.desc: Saves the current transform (use it with `restore`).

pyzed.draw.restore.desc: Goes back to the transform saved by the last `save`.

pyzed.draw.group.desc: Draws `shapes` translated, rotated and scaled without affecting the following shapes. Returns a list: expand it with `*`.

pyzed.designer.COMMON_EVENTS.desc: Events every control can handle in the designer's Events dock.
